- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

h14.

**Computation site**

The derived metadata is the memo's `Payload` (specifically `Payload.Tags` and `Payload.Property`), assembled by `RebuildMemoPayload` in `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`. That function delegates the actual content parsing to the markdown service's `ExtractAll` in `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356` (a single goldmark AST walk). `RebuildMemoPayload` copies the result onto the memo:

```go
memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
```
(`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:85-86`)

**Triggers (recomputation)**

- **Create** — every `CreateMemo` calls `RebuildMemoPayload` before persisting (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`).
- **Update, only when content changes** — `UpdateMemo` calls it inside the `path == "content"` branch of the update mask (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:436-451`); non-content updates (e.g. visibility) do not trigger it.
- **Backfill/batch rebuild** — the `Runner.RunOnce` job rebuilds the payload of all memos in batches of 100 (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27-72`, calling `RebuildMemoPayload` at line 52).

**Extracted properties**

From `ExtractAll` / `ExtractProperties` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:371-408`):

- **Tags** — deduplicated `#tags` (case preserved), excluding tags inside links/images (`markdown.go:376-378`, `418`).
- **Property.Title** — plain text of the first block if it's an H1 heading (`markdown.go:384-389`).
- **Property.HasLink** — true if any link node exists (`KindLink`).
- **Property.HasCode** — true for any code block, fenced code block, or inline code span.
- **Property.HasTaskList** — true if any task checkbox exists.
- **Property.HasIncompleteTasks** — true if any task checkbox is unchecked.

(The property set is defined by `storepb.MemoPayload_Property`: `Title`, `HasLink`, `HasCode`, `HasTaskList`, `HasIncompleteTasks`.) `ExtractAll` also gathers `Mentions`, but only `Tags` and `Property` are written back into the memo payload.

## Summary

This is the **memos** project (Go backend). Memo derived metadata is computed by a markdown-parsing service (goldmark-based) and stored in the memo's `Payload`. There is one important split: **tags + properties (incl. title)** are persisted in the payload and recomputed on write; the **snippet/preview** is generated on-the-fly at read time and not stored.

### 1. WHERE the metadata is computed

**Core extraction logic — `/bench/repo/internal/markdown/markdown.go`**

- `func (s *service) ExtractAll(content []byte) (*ExtractedData, error)` — lines **355-422**. The primary single-pass function. Walks the goldmark AST and populates an `ExtractedData` struct (`Tags`, `Mentions`, `Property`).
- `func (s *service) ExtractTags(content []byte) ([]string, error)` — lines **143-170**.
- `func (s *service) ExtractProperties(content []byte) (*storepb.MemoPayload_Property, error)` — lines **192-241**.
- `func (s *service) GenerateSnippet(content []byte, maxLength int) (string, error)` — lines **264-346** (plain-text preview generation).
- Helper `extractHeadingText` (lines 173-179) extracts the H1 title text.

`ExtractedData` struct (lines 20-25):
```go
type ExtractedData struct {
	Tags     []string
	Mentions []string
	Property *storepb.MemoPayload_Property
}
```

**Orchestration / where extraction is wired into a memo — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go`**

`func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error` — lines **74-88**:
```go
func RebuildMemoPayload(_ context.Context, memo *store.Memo, markdownService markdown.Service) error {
	if memo.Payload == nil {
		memo.Payload = &storepb.MemoPayload{}
	}
	// Use goldmark service to extract all metadata in a single pass (more efficient)
	data, err := markdownService.ExtractAll([]byte(memo.Content))
	if err != nil {
		return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to extract markdown metadata")
	}
	memo.Payload.Tags = data.Tags
	memo.Payload.Property = data.Property
	return nil
}
```

### 2. WHICH operations trigger recomputation

`RebuildMemoPayload` is invoked from three places:

- **On create** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` (inside the CreateMemo handler, before `s.Store.CreateMemo`).
- **On update, only when content changes** — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`. It runs only inside the `if path == "content"` branch of the update-mask loop (line 436), i.e. recomputation happens only when the `content` field is being updated; it then sets `update.Content` and `update.Payload` (lines 450-451). Updating other fields (e.g. visibility) does not recompute.
- **Bulk backfill/migration** — `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`, inside `Runner.RunOnce` (lines 27-72), which batches over all memos (100 at a time) and re-persists payloads. This is the one-time/maintenance rebuild path.

**Snippet (preview) is NOT stored/triggered on write** — it is generated at read/convert time:
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:83` — `getMemoContentSnippet` calls `GenerateSnippet([]byte(content), 64)` (max length 64).
- Called from the converter `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:76-80` (single memo) and lines 224-252 (batch relation snippets), assigned to `memoMessage.Snippet`.

### 3. WHAT the computation extracts

From `ExtractAll` (markdown.go lines 371-419), stored into `MemoPayload`:

- **Tags** (`data.Tags`) — all `#tags` from `TagNode`s (excluding tags inside links/images), deduplicated preserving case. Stored in `Payload.Tags`.
- **Mentions** (`data.Mentions`) — `@username` mentions, lowercased and deduped. (Note: `ExtractAll` returns these, but `RebuildMemoPayload` does not persist them into the payload; mentions are consumed separately via `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`.)
- **Property** (`data.Property`, type `storepb.MemoPayload_Property`) — stored in `Payload.Property`:
  - `Title` — text of the first block-level H1 heading, if the document's first block is an H1 (markdown.go lines 384-389 via `extractHeadingText`).
  - `HasLink` — true if any `KindLink` node exists.
  - `HasCode` — true if any code block / fenced code block / code span exists.
  - `HasTaskList` — true if any task checkbox exists.
  - `HasIncompleteTasks` — true if any unchecked task checkbox exists.

Proto definition of the stored payload — `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/memo.pb.go`: `MemoPayload` (lines 26-28: `Property`, `Tags`) and `MemoPayload_Property` (lines 85-92: `HasLink`, `HasTaskList`, `HasCode`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, `Title`).

The API-facing property conversion is `convertMemoPropertyFromStore` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_converter.go:315-326`, which exposes `HasLink`, `HasTaskList`, `HasCode`, `HasIncompleteTasks`, and `Title` (but not tags there — tags are copied directly at line 48).

### Snippet generation details (preview text)

`GenerateSnippet` (markdown.go 264-346) walks the AST, skips fenced/indented code blocks, concatenates text nodes (adding spaces between block elements), keeps `#tags` and autolink URLs, then truncates at a word boundary via `truncateAtWord` (lines 472-489), appending `" ..."` when truncated. Max length used by the API is 64 characters.</result>
